rounds.text: Coastal Roadways Ltd is trading at a heavily discounted valuation, sitting at a P/E of just 4.4x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 0.30x against a book value of ₹ 62.9 [E2], compared to sector benchmarks of 18.12x and 1.38x respectively [E6, E7]. This extreme disconnect is further highlighted by an EV/EBITDA of 0.95x versus a sector benchmark of 10.49x [E11], alongside a discounted cash flow intrinsic value estimate of ₹ 176 per share that leaves an 89.2% margin of safety [E43, E44]. Fundamental performance strongly outpaces market sentiment, evidenced by a 5-year profit growth of 35% dwarfing a 4% share price growth [E46], and a recent net profit surge of 750% YoY [E57] that signals a powerful operational turnaround. The balance sheet is exceptionally robust with zero debt at 0.00x debt-to-equity [E37], backed by strong cash generation including ₹ 2.44 Cr in operating cash flow and a healthy cash conversion of 1.56x for March 2026 [E34, E35]. Conceded: compounded 10-year sales growth is negative at -3% [E14] and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4].

Coastal Roadways Ltd exhibits severe, persistent top-line stagnation, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -3% and a poor 5-year sales growth rate of just 4.99% [E14, E53]. This lack of revenue expansion is accompanied by weak and underwhelming profitability returns, demonstrated by a 3-year median return on equity of only 8% and a low 3-year ROE average of 8.10% [E28, E54]. The market's deep skepticism toward these fundamentals is validated by brutal long-term shareholder wealth destruction, including a 1-year share price collapse of -49% and a 3-year compounded share price growth of -6% [E24, E25]. Furthermore, operating margins remain inconsistent across recent quarters and years, while quarterly operating margins compressed to 5% in September 2026 compared to 6% in the prior-year period [E31, E32, E33]. Compounding these fundamental and price performance concerns, despite reporting repeated profits, the company distributes a dividend yield of 0.00% and refuses to pay out dividends to shareholders [E4, E52]. Conceded: the company maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and generates positive operating cash flow alongside strong recent profit growth metrics [E35, E37, E57].

Conceded: 10-year compounded sales growth is -3% and 5-year sales growth is modest [E14, E53]. However, focusing solely on historical top-line stagnation ignores an accelerating earnings transformation where 5-year compounded profit growth hits 35%, 3-year profit growth reaches 30%, and TTM profit growth surges by 31% [E19, E20, E21], backed by recent screen metrics showing net profit up 750% year-on-year [E57]. Conceded: 3-year median return on equity is low at 8% and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E28, E52], but this ignores an exceptionally pristine balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x, flat zero borrowings, and robust operating cash flow of Rs 2.44 Cr with a stellar 1.56x cash conversion [E34, E35, E37, E38]. Conceded: recent quarterly operating margins compressed slightly to 5% and historical margins are inconsistent [E31, E32, E33], yet overall operating margins have expanded from 5% to 7% over a three-year span [E30]. Conceded: recent share price declines of -49% over 1 year and -6% over 3 years demonstrate deep market skepticism [E24, E25], but this price destruction occurs against a backdrop where fundamentals are massively outpacing the stock and a reverse DCF shows the current market price absurdly prices in a -14.7% earnings contraction [E45, E46].

The bull’s focus on profit growth ignores the reality that the company’s long-term sales trajectory remains fundamentally broken, with a 10-year compounded sales growth of -3% [E14] and a poor 5-year growth rate of 4.99% [E53]. While the bull highlights recent profit surges, these gains are occurring against a backdrop of inconsistent operating margins [E32, E33] and a recent quarterly margin contraction from 6% to 5% [E31]. Conceded: the company maintains a debt-free balance sheet [E37, E38, E50]. However, this conservative financing has not translated into shareholder value, as evidenced by a 10-year share price decline of -1% and a staggering -49% drop over the last year [E22, E25]. Furthermore, the bull’s reliance on a high intrinsic value estimate [E43] is undermined by the company’s persistent inability to generate meaningful returns for investors, evidenced by a low 3-year median ROE of 8% [E54] and a complete lack of dividend payouts [E4, E52]. Ultimately, the market’s deep skepticism, reflected in the stock trading at only 5% of its 52-week range [E5], suggests that the recent profit spikes may be viewed as unsustainable or insufficient to offset the company's long-term stagnation.
